headline: State Park Entry and Yurt Reservations
reservation: Entry is managed by Utah State Parks and may require a day-use fee at the gate. Overnight stays in the limited park yurts or developed campground should be booked months in advance via the official state portal to guarantee a spot in this remote desert location.

days.title: Introduction to the Goblins

stops.name: Valley of Goblins
stops.detail: Wander freely among thousands of mushroom-shaped sandstone hoodoos in the main valley floor.

stops.name: Observation Point
stops.detail: View the Three Sisters formation and get a panoramic perspective of the geological labyrinth.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours from Green River; conditions vary on Temple Mountain Road.
days.note: Wandering off-trail is permitted in the valley, but keep the overlook in sight to maintain orientation.

days.title: High Desert Benches

stops.name: Curtis Bench Trail
stops.detail: Follow the ridge for views of the Henry Mountains and the unique perspective of the valley below.

stops.name: Carmel Canyon
stops.detail: Explore the twisted eroded layers on this loop trail that highlights the park's diverse desert textures.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park; conditions vary by sand accumulation.
days.note: Desert heat can be intense by midday; plan your longer walks for the cooler morning hours.

days.title: San Rafael Swell Exploration

stops.name: Little Wild Horse Canyon
stops.detail: Experience a classic non-technical slot canyon just outside the park boundary.

stops.name: Bell Canyon
stops.detail: Complete the loop from Little Wild Horse for a full day of desert wash hiking.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to the trailhead; conditions vary on unpaved access roads.
days.note: Never enter slot canyons if there is any forecast of rain in the regional drainage area.

intel.title: Main Overlook Capacity
intel.text: The primary parking area near the goblins can fill during spring break and autumn weekends. Arrive before 10 AM to secure a spot near the valley stairs.

intel.title: Remote Desert Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect zero cellular reception once you turn off the main highway toward the park. A physical map or offline GPS is essential for navigating the San Rafael Swell area.

intel.title: Last Chance Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are unavailable at the park; the closest reliable services are in Hanksville or Green River. Check your gauges before departing these towns for the desert.

intel.title: Seasonal Heat Safety
intel.text: Summer temperatures often exceed 100°F with no natural shade in the valley. Spring and fall offer the safest hiking conditions for most travelers.

intel.title: Unpaved Road Conditions
intel.text: While the main road to the park is paved, many nearby sights in the Swell require driving on graded dirt. These roads can become impassable for all vehicles immediately following rain.

plan.arrival: Land at Canyonlands Regional Airport (CNY), rent a vehicle, and purchase all water and food supplies in Moab or Green River before heading west.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended for exploring the surrounding San Rafael Swell, though the main park road is accessible to cars.
plan.goldenHour: The Three Sisters formation provides dramatic silhouettes during the late afternoon desert glow.
